claims.text: The starting material is a tungsten-based WMoTaNb high-entropy alloy.
Spark plasma sintering at approximately 950°C and 50 MPa produces a homogeneous grain structure suitable for an intermediate plasma-facing layer.
Approximately 2 wt% chemically functionalized graphene nanoplatelets are added to the HEA powder before spark plasma sintering.
Surfactants or chemical functional groups will promote uniform GNP dispersion.
Chemical functionalization will promote strong bonding between the GNPs and the HEA matrix.
Sintering the modified material at approximately 950°C and 50 MPa will preserve the original HEA microstructure.
Functionalized GNPs will disperse uniformly along grain boundaries and within the HEA matrix.
The dispersed GNPs will form interconnected, high-conductivity pathways.
The GNPs will act as pinning sites that stabilize grain boundaries.
GNPs have sufficiently high intrinsic thermal conductivity to enhance heat transport in the alloy.
A percolative GNP network will facilitate rapid heat removal from the HEA.
Grain-boundary GNPs will inhibit grain-boundary sliding during thermal transients.
Grain-boundary GNPs will inhibit grain growth during thermal transients.
Chemical functionalization will produce a coherent interface with minimal stress concentration.
Adding approximately 2 wt% functionalized GNPs will improve overall thermal conductivity by approximately 25–30% relative to the unmodified tungsten-based HEA.
The GNP-modified alloy will retain mechanical strength under repeated thermal and mechanical cycling.
The GNP-modified alloy will retain ductility under repeated thermal and mechanical cycling.
Unmodified tungsten-based HEAs have limited thermal conductivity.
Unmodified tungsten-based HEAs are at risk of microstructural degradation under plasma-facing conditions.
The proposed performance will persist during cyclic loading up to 800°C, under high transient thermal gradients and cyclic mechanical loading.
